title: Lena and the Thorn
premise: Gideon Winterbourne, exiled from her storm-calling order for refusing to weaponize a child's soul, has spent nine years hiding as a ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things. When a mute girl named Lena arrives speaking the First Tongue—the language that binds souls to contracts—Gideon realizes Lena is the collateral on a debt her own family sold generations ago to the court beneath the mountain. To free her, Gideon must steal back the original contract from the Undercourt before the solstice sealing, betraying both her guild and the lover she left behind among the storm-callers. She succeeds at terrible cost: her exile is lifted, but she chooses to remain with Lena and her found family, tearing up her inheritance rather than claim it.
about_author: Marguerite Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three collections of books that technically did not exist. She writes fantasy about bureaucratic magic and the people who fall through its cracks.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A rain-soaked child appears at the guild door during inventory night, speaking a language Gideon recognizes from forbidden childhood lessons: the First Tongue. When Lena touches a ledger, entries rewrite themselves around her name. Gideon hides the girl from the guildmaster, discovering in old family records that Winterbournes sold a soul-debt centuries ago—and Lena is the payment come due. Beat: dread blooming into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Owes
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon and Lena's POV (Lena's chapters rendered in fragmented First Tongue translations). Gideon bargains with the guild for passage down, while Lena begins remembering lives she never lived—memories leaking from the soul bound inside her. An old guild rival offers help at a price: Gideon's storm-calling sigil, surrendered forever. Beat: the cost of love made concrete; Gideon pays it.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, climax. In the Undercourt, Gideon faces the Archivist of Debts—a mirror-faced thing wearing her grandmother's voice—and learns her exile was engineered to keep her bloodline's contract enforceable. Her former lover, now a storm-caller enforcer, arrives to drag her home but instead holds the court's guards at bay. Gideon burns the contract using the last of her stolen lightning, shattering the seal. Beat: betrayal revealed, love chosen over duty at the point of no return.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Rain
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, resolution. Above ground at solstice dawn, Lena speaks her first words in the common tongue: Gideon's name. The guild grudgingly makes them both members; the storm-callers offer Gideon reinstatement, and she declines, signing her inheritance over to fund Lena's schooling. The final image: two ledgers side by side—one of debts erased, one just begun. Beat: quiet joy; family is what you write your own name into.
